name: What if there is an old pool under a patio or deck?

mainEntity.name: Can contractors remove a pool when it is partially covered by concrete, pavers, or a deck?
mainEntity.text: Can contractors remove a pool when it is partially covered by concrete, pavers, or a deck?

acceptedAnswer.text: A pool hidden under a patio, deck, or other hardscape is more complex than a visible open pool. The contractor may need to remove pavers, stamped concrete, wood decking, or built-in features before the actual pool demolition can begin. That adds labor, disposal, and restoration work to the project. It also increases the chance of uncovering drainage issues or hidden utilities. Homeowners should ask whether the bid includes removal and replacement of the covering surface or only the pool shell beneath it. If the goal is to reclaim the entire backyard, the full scope should cover both demolition layers and final grading. Projects like this often require a site visit because the structure above the pool can change access and reveal extra work that is not obvious from the surface.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but removing a pool under a patio or deck usually adds demolition, hauling, and restoration costs. The contractor must first remove the covering surface, then demolish the pool shell and rebuild or regrade the area afterward.
